name: calendar
description: Calendars display days, weeks, and months, allowing users to select dates or ranges. One to three months are shown side by side (option visibleMonths). Also called RangeCalendar when selectionMode is range.

documentBlocks.content: Calendars display days, weeks, and months, allowing users to select dates or ranges. One to three months are shown side by side (option visibleMonths). Also called RangeCalendar when selectionMode is range.

Unavailable dates.

When a day or several days are unavailable within the calendar popover, each day should display a strikethrough to help the user understand that they cannot select it. Disabled days use a distinct gray style to clearly differentiate them from unavailable days. When the calendar prevents selection of past dates, this visual treatment helps users distinguish disabled days from those marked as unavailable.

Why unavailable and disabled days are necessary.

In a date selection system, users often need to distinguish between dates that cannot be selected and dates that are simply inactive. Supporting both states improves clarity and prevents errors. Here's an example scenario: A potential guest is browsing a calendar to book a stay at a vacation rental. Unavailable dates: Days when the rental is already booked or blocked by the owner. These appear with a strikethrough, indicating they cannot be selected. Disabled dates: Past dates that are no longer valid for booking. These appear visually distinct (gray style) to show they are inactive. Guests see unavailable dates marked clearly so they don't attempt to select them. Hosts or admins can view past dates as disabled and also mark future dates as unavailable when needed. By supporting both behaviors, the system provides a clear, intuitive experience for different user roles and prevents confusion during date selection.

Range fill color.

The range fill shows which days fall between two selected dates. If the range spans more than the three-month calendar view, it ends on the last visible day but continues as users navigate with the calendar chevrons. A dashed stroke outlines the fill to improve visibility on bright screens and for users with vision impairments.
Do not change the styling of unavailable days
documentBlocks.dont: The strikethrough styling intentionally accommodates internationalization.

documentBlocks.content:
Calendar popover states.

The calendar popover supports a disabled state but not a read-only state. Dates or months may be temporarily disabled based on context (for example, if a user must complete a task before selecting a date). In these cases, help text can explain why certain dates are unavailable. If a date picker is truly read-only, users shouldn't be able to open the calendar popover at all, since they can't interact with it.

Optional time fields.

The calendar popover can also include time-specific fields, allowing users to specify start and end times.

currentMonth.description: The month currently displayed in the calendar (1 = January, 12 = December).

currentYear.description: The year currently displayed in the calendar (Gregorian year number).

selectionMode.description: Controls whether the calendar allows selecting a single date or a date range. A range adds the range-fill band behind the days between the two selected dates.

visibleMonths.description: How many months the calendar shows side by side: one, two or three. The engine draws one month per entry of the months option, so a request supplies that many entries.

months.description: The months drawn side by side. Each entry is one copy of the month part, so the number of entries is the number of months drawn; visibleMonths names the intended count (one to three) but does not set it.

title.description: Month and year text of the month.

days.description: The cells of the month's day grid, in order, same shape as the days option. A leading cell with an empty label (label "") and no date is a blank cell that keeps the first weekday column; a cell with no label field draws the month title as its text.

weekdays.description: The weekday headings above each month's day grid, seven entries in the week's order (firstDayOfWeek is the data's choice).

isSelected.description: Whether the rendered day is selected (Figma .Day Type=Selected; in a range, every day from start to end). Per-day in a data-driven calendar is days[].isSelected.

isRangeStart.description: Whether the rendered day is the start of the selected range (React Spectrum isSelectionStart). Per-day is days[].isRangeStart.

isRangeEnd.description: Whether the rendered day is the end of the selected range (React Spectrum isSelectionEnd). Per-day is days[].isRangeEnd.

isUnavailable.description: Whether the rendered day is unavailable (Figma .Day Type=Unavailable, React Spectrum isUnavailable). Per-day is days[].isUnavailable.

isToday.description: Whether the rendered day is today (Figma Current day indicator). Per-day is days[].isToday.

minValue.description: The minimum allowed date that a user may select (ISO format string).

maxValue.description: The maximum allowed date that a user may select (ISO format string).

days.description: An array of days displayed in the current calendar view.

date.description: The date represented by this day (ISO format string).

label.description: The day number text drawn in the cell.

isSelected.description: Whether this day is currently selected.

isRangeStart.description: Whether this day is the start of a selected range.

isRangeEnd.description: Whether this day is the end of a selected range.

isUnavailable.description: Whether this day is unavailable for selection. If true, the day appears with a strikethrough.

isToday.description: Whether this day represents the current date.

state.description: The interaction state of the day cell.

slots.name: default
slots.description: The visible months. Each entry of the months option is drawn as one copy of the month part, side by side.

slots.name: weekday-label
slots.description: The weekday headings. Each entry of the weekdays option is drawn as one copy of the weekday-label part, seven to a row.

slots.name: day
slots.description: The day cells of a month. Each entry of the month's days field is drawn as one copy of the day part.

anatomy.name: container
anatomy.description: Root of the calendar: holds the previous and next buttons, the months and the help text, and owns the 24 gap between months. It draws no surface of its own; the popover that holds a calendar is part of the component that opens it (date-picker nests a popover part).

anatomy.name: previous-button
anatomy.description: Quiet action-button (component action-button with isQuiet true) that moves to the previous month. Drawn on the first visible month.

anatomy.name: next-button
anatomy.description: Quiet action-button (component action-button with isQuiet true) that moves to the next month. Drawn on the last visible month.

anatomy.name: month
anatomy.description: One visible month: its title, its weekday grid and its day grid. Repeated once per entry of the months option.

anatomy.name: title
anatomy.description: Month and year text of a month (Figma Month + Year, RSP CalendarHeading).

anatomy.name: weekday-grid
anatomy.description: Seven-column grid of a month's weekday labels.

anatomy.name: day-grid
anatomy.description: Seven-column grid of a month's days, with blank leading cells so the first day lands under its weekday.

anatomy.name: weekday-label
anatomy.description: Single-letter weekday heading cell in a month's weekday grid. Seven per month.

anatomy.name: text
anatomy.description: Weekday letter drawn in a weekday-label cell (Figma Days of week Value).

anatomy.name: day
anatomy.description: One date cell of a month's day grid. Styled for selected, hover, error, disabled and unavailable.

anatomy.name: day-fill
anatomy.description: Circle behind the day number: the selected, hover, keyboard-focus and error fill of a day (Figma .Day Calendar Day frame). Drawn over the range-fill band, under the label.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.description: Day number text of a day cell (Figma .Day Value, RSP CalendarCell text).

anatomy.name: current-day-indicator
anatomy.description: Marker that sets today's cell apart. Drawn inside the day when its isToday is true.

anatomy.name: unavailable-indicator
anatomy.description: Line struck through the day number of an unavailable day (Figma strikethrough). Drawn inside the day when its isUnavailable is true.

anatomy.name: range-fill
anatomy.description: Highlight band behind a day inside a selected range (Figma .Range fill Highlight fill, selection background). It sits under the day circle, so the band of consecutive days reads as one band; the days at the two ends are rounded on the outer side. Drawn only when selectionMode is range and the day is selected.

anatomy.name: help-text
anatomy.description: Component part: the help-text component, shown with an error message below the calendar when isError is true.

anatomy.name: focus-indicator
anatomy.description: Outline drawn around the focused day.

anatomyReview.notes: A9 (2026-11-21), owner decisions C2, C3, C4, C8, C10 to C15. calendar is the only anatomy; single-, double- and triple-calendar are frozen legacy holders and visibleMonths 1|2|3 replaces them. It draws no popover (date-picker nests the popover). Months are the repeated month part (months collection slot); each holds a title, a weekday-grid and a day-grid, each grid a collection slot. Nested components (action-button, help-text) are described, not declared: the anatomy component field is not built. range-fill is described as visible for selectionMode range because presentIn takes states, not options. Figma has no Calendar page (Date picker page only); RSP S2 Calendar.
